title: The Rain and the Snow
skill_description: Practice reading common vowel team patterns for long vowels: ai (rain), ay (play), ee (tree), ea (read), oa (boat), ow (snow).
author: FunBookies
summary: When rain turns to snow, a girl named Jean dreams of playing outside. She waits for the snow to stay, then plays in the snow with her goat named Gray.

pages.text: The Rain and the Snow
pages.scene: A girl looking out a window at rain turning to snow, a gray goat visible outside. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Words to Know
Jean woke up and saw the rain fall. She said, "I need to wait."
pages.scene: A girl looking out a rainy window with disappointment. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: The rain came down on the road. It fell on the green tree too.
pages.scene: Rain falling on a road and green trees outside a house. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean said, "I dream of a snow day! I would play in the snow!"
pages.scene: A thought bubble showing the girl playing in snow. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean sat by the window. She could see her goat Gray eat hay.
pages.scene: Jean watching a gray goat eating hay in the rain. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: The rain began to slow. Jean said, "May the rain stay away!"
pages.scene: Rain slowing down, girl looking hopeful. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Then Jean saw snow! The snow came to stay. It was a very cold day.
pages.scene: Snow beginning to fall, replacing the rain. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean got her coat. She said, "I need to play in the snow!"
pages.scene: Jean putting on her warm winter coat excitedly. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean ran to Gray the goat. Gray was by the road in the snow.
pages.scene: Jean running toward her gray goat standing in the snowy road. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean and Gray made a trail in the snow. They could see their feet!
pages.scene: Jean and Gray walking through snow, leaving footprints. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean said, "The snow is so clean and white! I know it will grow!"
pages.scene: Jean looking up at more snow falling from the sky. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Gray ran slow in the deep snow. Jean had to wait for Gray.
pages.scene: The goat moving slowly through deep snow while Jean waits. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: They sat by the tree. Jean gave Gray a treat. He likes oats the best!
pages.scene: Jean and Gray resting under a snowy tree, Jean feeding the goat. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean said, "I should keep you free to roam, Gray. You need a way home."
pages.scene: Jean looking at Gray with care, pointing toward the barn. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean and Gray went to the road. They saw the snow glow in the low sun.
pages.scene: Jean and Gray walking down a snowy road at sunset, snow glowing. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean said, "This was a dream day! The rain went and the snow came to stay!"
pages.scene: Jean hugging Gray happily in the snow. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean went home to sleep. She would dream of snow and play with Gray.
pages.scene: Jean sleeping peacefully in bed, dream clouds showing snow and Gray. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: The rain may come back, but the snow will too. Jean and Gray will play!
pages.scene: A view of the snowy yard with the goat in the barn, moonlight glowing. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: Jean knows the best days are with her goat Gray, rain or snow.
pages.scene: Jean and Gray together on a beautiful snowy morning. Warm watercolor style.

pages.text: The End
pages.scene: Jean and Gray silhouetted against a sunset over snowy hills. Warm watercolor style.

parent_tips.before_reading: Preview the cover of 'The Rain and the Snow'. Ask: What do you think will happen? Look for words with reading skills.
parent_tips.during_reading: When you see tricky words, help your child sound them out. Notice words that use reading skills.
parent_tips.after_reading: Ask: What was the problem in the story? How was it solved? What did May learn?
